text:
ana: Quick thread — we need a razor-sharp battlecard for the webinar next Wed. Focus: head-to-head narrative vs cloud AI endpoints + clear inbound routing for signups. TL;DR: 1) hero claim 2) benchmark snippet 3) routing rule 4) demo talking points

mike: Love it. Can we make the hero claim about predictable cost and fallback reliability (not just raw speed)? customers care about 'stability when traffic spikes' more than peak FLOPS. :thumbsup:

julia: Agree. Suggest hero: 'Predictable inference economics across hosted, dedicated, and private.' Short and punchy.

sam: For benchmark snippet — keep it an apples-to-apples latency+cost line: e.g., 6x lower 95th percentile latency on multimodal prompts, 2.3x token cost reduction with prefix caching. We should cite our infra config (a2/rtx/quantized) in small text.

ana: @sam quick: can you draft 1-sentence benchmark blurb we can paste in the slide?
sam: "In our internal eval on a 1k-user tail workload, Redwood delivered 95th percentile latency 6x lower than a leading cloud-managed endpoint and reduced per-token compute by 2.3x via smart KV caching and batching." — tag me for edits.

kai: For demo flow, propose 3-step: 1) baseline cloud endpoint w/ cold-start visible 2) switch to Redwood hosted (same model) to show steady tail 3) toggle to Dedicated to show throughput bump + routing fallback. Keep each step <90s.

mike: Nice. For inbound routing: we need a deterministic rule to route demo requests and hand-raisers. Proposal: high-intent leads (webinar form selects 'enterprise' or >$50k ARR) -> Sales AEs, all others -> SDR nurture. Also route any compliance/regulatory checkboxes to Solutions Eng.

routing-bot: rule-preview:
```
if form.size == 'enterprise' or form.estimated_spend >= 50000:
  route -> sales_ae_team
elif form.compliance_flag == true:
  route -> solutions_eng
else:
  route -> sdr_nurture
```

julia: Can we add a workshop CTA on the follow-up email for those routed to SE? 'Book a 1:1 workshop to validate private deployment constraints' — this helps surface Private deals.

ana: Copy deck note: avoid naming specific cloud vendors in hero claim; instead use 'managed endpoints' or 'cloud-managed inference' to keep it legal-friendly. We can call out competitors in appendix with source links.

sam: Also include two quick rebut bullets: 1) 'Why not just use vanilla endpoints?' — answer: operational complexity + unpredictable tail. 2) 'Why not self-host?' — answer: ops cost and lack of standardized rollout + SLA.

mike: Who owns the one-pager? I'll capture routing + CTAs. @julia please do 2x hero variants (short/long). @sam please finalize the benchmark sentence and a tiny notes box with infra config. @ana will own deck flow and demo script.

ana: Sounds good. Aim to have first drafts by EOD Friday so we can rehearse Monday. I'll schedule a 30m playtest Tue morning. :calendar:

kai: Quick note for webinar ops: we'll need network logs and demo keys ready in staging. Ping eng-runtime for a smoke test on Monday.

mike: Thanks all — if anyone wants to add example copy for the follow-up email or landing page, drop it here and I'll fold it in.

julia: dropping two punchlines now: 1) 'Inference that scales with your business, not your headaches.' 2) 'Same API, predictable economics, enterprise-grade controls.' Feedback welcome.

ana: Love both — will pick one for slide headlines and keep the other for email subject lines. Closing the loop: drafts by Friday, playtest Tue. :rocket:
